functional_sequences.mechanism: Polarized acinar epithelium stores secretory products apically and releases into its lumen.
steps: Identify one cell boundary and basal nucleus; explain protein synthesis without claiming RER geometry.
Show apical cytoplasm and separately named granules within the same owner.
State cholinergic stimulus and a schematic Ca2+ signal; CCK-related human responsiveness remains qualified.
Move/shrink granule cue at apical membrane and reveal receiving lumen plus centroacinar duct origin.
schematic_limitations: No membrane fusion machinery, organelle synthesis kinetics or measured secretion rate.
Shrinking represents fusion, and markers/cells are enlarged.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Acinar products drain through successive duct levels; duct epithelium adds bicarbonate-rich fluid.
steps: Retain duct walls in section while shared final centerlines carry juice cues.
Identify separate secretin-driven ductal bicarbonate/water response with CFTR-associated transport.
Trace into intralobular/interlobular drainage; explain off-specimen intestinal destination and protease activation.
schematic_limitations: Ion transport is an explanation unless a marked magnified inset is constructed.
Existing particles are not a conserved fluid solver; no pressure or secretory-volume computation.
Interlobular juice cue requires source integration if the full displayed route is claimed.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Beta-cell glucose-triggered secretion transfers hormone to nearby capillary blood, distinct from exocrine lumen delivery.
steps: Expose mixed representative human endocrine tissue with retained owner membranes and nuclei.
State independent increased glucose, metabolism/ATP, KATP closure, depolarization and Ca2+ entry.
Use sampled actual beta-owner membrane-to-nearby-capillary transfer path.
Then show hormone transport within receiving blood, retaining capillary walls in section.
schematic_limitations: Hormone cue is not a vesicle crossing intact endothelium.
The simplified triggering path omits amplifying pathways and measured glycemic responses.
No universal beta-core/alpha-mantle or islet-first microvascular ordering.
A four-second comparison period is not human secretion kinetics.

functional_sequences.mechanism: A representative interconnected vascular route supplies pancreatic tissue, permits exchange and drains toward veins.
steps: Identify representative connected endocrine/exocrine capillary exchange domain.
Distinguish constructed vascular junctions from projected tube crossings and specimen cuts.
Trace an authored representative venous outlet, explain off-specimen portal/liver drainage.
schematic_limitations: Dybala et al. human topology evidence and mouse bidirectional-flow measurements are distinguished.
No universal ordering, endothelial permeability or CFD model is inferred.
A new connected route must be validated from emitted saved meshes.
